extracted.intended_audience: Authors preparing and submitting manuscripts to PeerJ (including PeerJ Computer Science)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing, formatting, and submitting manuscripts (research articles, literature reviews, AI Applications, Data Reports) to PeerJ, including files, data/code deposition, figures/tables, and ethical/permission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear, unambiguous, technically and grammatically correct English
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use clear, unambiguous, technically and grammatically correct English throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either English or American spelling is acceptable provided it is used consistently. The established norms of academic writing within your field should be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission files
rubrics_metrics.description: Files: Manuscript, Figures, Tables, Raw data or code files. Data or code is almost always required for review and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw data and/or code must be submitted as either: (a) a link to an immutable repository with a DOI, or (b) Supplemental file(s) if filesize < 30 MB. Files must be machine-readable (PDF, PowerPoint, images etc. are not accepted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and code deposition and persistent identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data and code must be accessible via an immutable repository and/or supplemental files; software on social coding platforms must be archived in an archival repository that provides DOIs (e.g., Zenodo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GitHub repositories can be archived directly by Zenodo. GitLab repositories must be 'released', downloaded as a .zip and uploaded to Zenodo to obtain a DOI. If using previously published author-written or third-party code, it must be cited appropriately with a persistent identifier (DOI or Software Heritage ID) when available. If third-party code lacks a PID, the code writer(s) MUST be acknowledged and authors should attempt to make the code findable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linked repositories must contain exact copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Linked data and/or code repositories must contain an exact copy of what was used to perform the study described within the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Zenodo supports DOI versioning allowing a DOI to be obtained for specific versions so datasets/code can be built upon without disturbing replicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental files — types and size limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental Files are files not part of the main manuscript (e.g. raw data, code, large datasets, figures, videos). Supplemental Files should not exceed 50 MB in total (30MB individual file limit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more space please contact PeerJ. Files intended for review but not publication can be uploaded as Review-only info Supplemental Files. Supplemental files must be understandable by an English language reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental file naming and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the file naming format 'Supplemental [Item] S[number]' (e.g. 'Supplemental Data S1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the following style when citing Supplemental files in the text: Fig. S1, Table S1, Data S1, Video S1, Article S1, Audio S1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting — page and layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript formatting: US Letter; use line numbers; 2.5 cm margin on all edges; 12 point Times font for readability; 'Normal' style for text, 'Heading' styles for headings; do not use 'unusual' document styles/templates; left justify all text (do not full width justify).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use line numbers to aid review. If final typeset page count exceeds 40 pages an additional service charge may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Be clear, appealing, interesting and specific. Match the search queries used to find similar articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise: ideally 20-60 words (250 character hard limit). Avoid acronyms, abbreviations and jargon. Accurately describe work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract: 500 word (3,000 character) limit. Self-contained, concise description of reason for the work, methodology, results, and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncommon abbreviations should be spelled out at first use. No footnotes or references (except when referencing a critiqued publication by DOI). Subheadings in abstract must be bold, followed by a period, and start a new paragraph (e.g., Background.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard sections for Research Article
rubrics_metrics.description: Use these Standard Sections where possible. Do not combine sections. Research Article standard section list: Author Cover Page, Abstract, Background, [methodology/experimental sections appropriate to your work], Results, Discussion, Conclusions, Acknowledgments, References.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not acknowledge funders in Acknowledgments (there is a separate Funding Statement). Everyone named in Acknowledgments must be informed that they are named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature Review structure and survey methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Literature Review standard sections: Author Cover Page, Abstract, Introduction, Survey Methodology, Subheadings, Conclusions, Acknowledgments, References.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction should describe the field and explain why the review is needed and its relevance. Survey Methodology should explain how you ensured comprehensive and unbiased coverage of the literature. Subheadings: subdivide into a small number of major topic areas. Conclusions: identify unresolved questions/gaps/future directions. Also read the policies for literature reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI Application article mandatory elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must include the following criteria in their submission for it to be considered an AI Application article: place requirements at authors' discretion within manuscript; all code implemented must be uploaded as supplementary files or at a persistent DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction: include motivations for both the study and the techniques used. Materials & Methods: include name and source (DOI/URL) of any 3rd party datasets; describe data preprocessing; explain selection method for techniques; provide computing infrastructure details (OS, hardware, software); include evaluation method and assessment metrics and justify them. Results & Discussion: present findings clearly using figures/tables; interpret results and compare with existing research using the assessment metrics. Conclusions: explain and justify the model type; identify limitations and future directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Report standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Data Reports should follow the Research Article format as far as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Author Cover Page and appropriate sections per Research Article guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Cover Page requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Author Cover Page included as the first page of the manuscript. Author info entered online must exactly match the author info listed on the Author Cover Page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author Cover Page structure: Article title; Authors (first given names or initials with middle name initials; family name); Affiliations (department, university/organization, location city/state/province, country). Submission admin contact (first and last name, email). If authored by a consortium, list names and affiliations in correct order in the Acknowledgments section. All authors must meet the ICMJE authorship requirements. Include other contributors in Acknowledgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: No cover letters or pre-submission inquiries required
rubrics_metrics.description: No cover letters or pre-submission inquiries needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ready to submit? Login or create a PeerJ.com account to begin your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / prior publication restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot publish any materials that have been published in a peer-reviewed journal previously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of prior peer review from other journals is allowed (see separate guidance) but prior peer-reviewed publication is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference formatting policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose your style; PeerJ prefers authors spend time doing science not formatting references. Submit references in whatever style you like, but they must be full, clear, and consistent; PeerJ will standardize at production. PeerJ uses the 'Name. Year' style with an alphabetized reference list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal reference format example and many examples provided. All citations must be present in the reference section, and all references cited in the text. Place non-cited references in a 'Further Reading' section. Zotero/EndNote/Mendeley guidance provided for PeerJ style.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-text citation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For three or fewer authors, list all author names (e.g. Smith, Jones & Johnson, 2004). For four or more, abbreviate with ‘first author’ et al. (e.g. Smith et al., 2005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple references to the same item should be separated with a semicolon (;) and ordered chronologically. References by the same author in the same year should be differentiated by letters (Smith, 2001a; Smith, 2001b). Cite articles accepted for publication as 'in press' and upload as a Supplemental file. Cite unpublished work as 'unpublished data' in-text and do not include it in the reference section. Avoid referencing personal communications; reference as 'pers. comm.' including first initial, surname and year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference section ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference Section sorted by Author, Year, Title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All citations must be present in the reference section, and all references cited in the text. Place non-cited references in a 'Further Reading' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table formatting and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables must be editable. Do not upload tables as images. Tables must fit a US Letter page with 2.5 cm margins. Include units in parentheses in column and row headings. Place footnotes below the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred file type DOCX; other acceptable types DOC, ODT, TEX. Table text should be roman black text. Special significance may be indicated by bold/italic/underline — explain formatting in the table legend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file types and image quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the original file format and image size whenever possible. Prefer vector images where possible; suitable vector types: EPS, PDF (US Letter, 2.5cm margins). For raster images (photographs, micrographs, screenshots) preferred formats are PNG (preferred) and JPEG (photographs only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideal width/height: 3000px (minimum 900px). Upload figures as separate files (do not embed in manuscript). Lower quality images may be accepted for review but must be replaced with high-quality (300 dpi) images on resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure and table filenames and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Name your figures 'Figure1.png', 'Figure2.jpg', etc. Name your tables 'Table1.docx', 'Table2.docx', etc. Figure 1 appears first in the text and first cited, Figure 2 appears second and next cited, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include figure/table numbers in filenames. When citing use the abbreviation 'Fig.'; when starting a sentence with a citation use 'Figure 1'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles and legends for figures and tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles are required for all figures (legends are optional). Titles are required for all tables (legends optional). Figure legends should be self contained and clearly describe the figure and its contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles and legends below the image can be included in the image file for first review; titles and legends must be removed for re-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multipart figures and multi-page images
rubrics_metrics.description: Multipart figures: image parts combined and submitted as one file. Multi-part or single images should not span multiple pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multi-part figures submitted in one file and arranged as they are to be published. Minimum white space around each figure/figure part. Label with readable, uniform font; vertical height of 2mm suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image whitespace, orientation and filenames
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove all whitespace around images. Upload images in correct orientation. Landscape is preferable in most cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name files according to the Figure/Table naming conventions. Ensure minimum white space and correct orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image content requirements (axes, scales, units)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include scales, abbreviations, limits, units of measure, etc. in the graphical area of the image. All X and Y-axes must have accompanying units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure legends should be self-contained. When creating figures consider accessibility of color schemes to those with non-normal color vision; avoid using color alone to distinguish parts of images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal image processing and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be minimally processed/manipulated, to add labels, arrows, or change contrast (applied to whole image inc. controls). Do not adjust in any way that could lead to misinterpretation of the information in the original image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unprocessed figure files and data must be retained for editorial review upon request. Descriptions of changes and hardware and software used to take the images and make adjustments must also be provided. Inappropriate figure manipulation is grounds for article retraction and reporting to institutional oversight boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on hand-drawn figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand-drawn figures are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce figures in acceptable digital formats per the figure file type guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility guidance for figures (color use)
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating figures and images consider the accessibility of your chosen color schemes to those with non-normal color vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wherever possible avoid using color alone to distinguish between parts of images. Consult resources such as R Cookbook, Mapbox and ColorBrewer for maximum accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and third-party content permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Your article is published under a CC BY licence, so any images or content with a more restrictive licence requires permission and/or referencing. Reference copyright holders in figure legends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 3rd party photography upload a completed photographer's permission letter as a supplementary file. For 3rd party maps, include map data attribution in the image and the legend (e.g., 'Map data © 2026 Google'). Use maps which allow unrestricted re-use where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission for recognisable faces and minors
rubrics_metrics.description: For images containing recognisable faces add a permission statement in the note to staff for each person depicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided permission text. If the person is under the age of 16, consent should be given by a parent or guardian. Per ICMJE, measures such as blurring faces or masking the eye region in photographs of patients is inadequate protection of anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript filetypes accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript document formats accepted: .DOCX (Preferred) and .DOC, .TeX (+ PDF with embedded figures and tables), .ODT, .RTF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: US Letter, line numbers, 2.5 cm margins, 12 point Times font, 'Normal' style for text, 'Heading' styles for headings, left-justified text. For LaTeX submissions submit a single PDF with full set of LaTeX source files.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX submission specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeX: Submit a single PDF with the full set of LaTeX source files. Use line numbers. Overleaf is recommended and templates are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TeX / LaTeX users: submit your complete PDF manuscript, TEX, BIB, hi-res figures and tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw data/code availability and recommended repositories
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are responsible for making materials, code, raw data and associated protocols relevant to the submission available without delay. Data or code should be submitted to a specialist database if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended repositories include institutional repositories, Zenodo (free & unlimited), Figshare (20GB free), Dryad, Galaxy server, Git Large File Storage, GitHub (code), GitLab (code). For review-only (move to persistent depository on publication): Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive. pan.baidu.com cannot be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental multimedia file formats and playback
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental Videos: submit as AVI, MOV, WMV, and MP4. Supplemental Audio: submit as WAV or MP3 files and include a legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For video provide 128 kbit/s AAC audio and 480p H.264 video in an MPEG-4 (mp4) format for widest compatibility, and check that files open/play in recent versions of QuickTime and Windows Media Player. Ensure audio files open and play in common audio players such as iTunes or Windows Media Player.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large supplemental datasets handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Supplemental Data sets should be submitted in a compressed format (e.g., zip or tar.gz).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental files are published alongside the article but are not integral to it. Titles are required for all supplemental items. Supplemental Files should not exceed 50 MB in total (30MB individual file limit). If you need more space contact PeerJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission from external services
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ Computer Science welcomes submissions directly from external services with one-click submission routes from bioRxiv, Overleaf, and Peerage of Science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once submission is transferred staff will initiate submission for you and contact you to complete final information and confirm submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration and reuse of prior peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ Computer Science is happy to use prior peer-reviews which have been conducted on a manuscript (e.g., reviewed by another journal) which can increase speed of decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain written permission from the other journal to use these reviews and upload it as a Supplemental File. Alert staff in 'Notes to Staff' field that you have prior reviews and upload them as an external reviews file type. Provide a document detailing changes made in light of these reviews. Staff will contact the other journal to confirm reviews are complete and unedited and request permission to use them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission guidance availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission guidance documents are provided — download the appropriate Guidance PDFs for resubmission and for LaTeX resubmissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided resubmission guidance PDFs when preparing a resubmission.
